summary.text: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) separates carbon dioxide from a large source such as a gas processing plant and moves it to long-term storage, typically in a deep geological formation.
About 80% of captured CO₂ is pumped into partly depleted oil reservoirs to extract more oil, which is why it is also called CCUS.
As of 2024 it ran at 44 plants catching about a thousandth of global CO₂ emissions, while cheaper options like solar and wind cut air pollution far more.

facts.label: Oil and gas link
facts.value: About 90% of operations involve that industry

facts.label: Unbuilt projects
facts.value: About 70% of announced projects never materialized

items.prompt: Captured CO₂ from a gas plant is sold to an oil company. What is it most likely used for?

options.label: Making fizzy drinks for sale
Injecting into old oil fields to get more oil out
Turning into plastic packaging
Feeding greenhouses to grow crops

items.explain: Around 80% of captured CO₂ goes to enhanced oil recovery, where it is injected into partly depleted reservoirs to extract more oil.

items.prompt: A power plant adds CCS equipment. What happens to the amount of fuel it burns to run?

options.label: It falls, since the plant runs cleaner
It stays exactly the same
It goes up, because capture uses energy
It drops to zero once storage begins

items.explain: Plants with CCS need more energy to operate, so they typically burn additional fossil fuel.

items.prompt: A company captures CO₂ and turns it into fuel that is later burned in trucks. Why does this not count as CCS?

options.label: The carbon is released again when the fuel burns
Fuel making is banned for captured gas
The CO₂ was not captured from a factory
Trucks run on electricity instead

items.explain: CCS requires long-term storage, and products such as fuel release CO₂ again when burned.

items.prompt: As of 2024, roughly what fraction of the world's carbon dioxide emissions did all CCS plants together capture?

options.label: About one-half
About one-tenth
About one-hundredth
About one-thousandth

items.explain: The 44 operating plants captured about one-thousandth of global carbon dioxide emissions.

items.prompt: A city wants the cheapest way to cut emissions that also cleans its air the most. Compared with CCS, how do options like solar, wind and public transit rate?

options.label: Cheaper and better at reducing air pollution
Cheaper but worse at reducing air pollution
Costlier and better at reducing air pollution
Costlier and worse at reducing air pollution

items.explain: Solar, wind, electrification and public transit are less expensive than CCS and much more effective at reducing air pollution.

items.prompt: The processes behind CCS were first used by oil and gas companies. What were they mainly used for back then?

options.label: Cutting greenhouse gas emissions
Cleaning city air near refineries
Purifying natural gas and boosting oil output
Storing fuel safely for wartime

items.explain: Early CCS technologies mainly purified natural gas and increased oil production; climate use was discussed later.
